content: 1. Preventive chemotherapy is recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) to manage soil-transmitted helminth infections in populations at risk, as outlined in their 2017 publication. 2. The WHO released guidelines in 2022 focusing on the control and elimination of human schistosomiasis. 3. A systematic review conducted by Fisher et al. in 2012 examined the prevalence and factors influencing common perinatal mental disorders in women from lowand lower-middle-income countries, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 4. Muzik, Thelen, and Rosenblum (2011) discussed the detection and treatment of perinatal depression in their publication in Neuropsychiatry. 5. Andermann et al. (2008) revisited Wilson and Jungner's screening criteria in the genomic era, reviewing developments over the past 40 years, as published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 6. Waqas et al. (2022) systematically reviewed evidence on screening programs for maternal mental health disorders among perinatal women, with findings published in BMC Psychiatry. 7. Morrell et al. (2009) conducted a cluster-randomized trial and economic evaluation of psychological interventions for postnatal depression, known as the PoNDER trial, published in Health Technology Assessment. 8. The WHO and Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation (2014) explored the social determinants of mental health in their Geneva publication. 9. Smith, Portela, and Harvey conducted a scoping review on global policies and guidelines for discharge preparation and readiness after birth, with findings published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 10. Armstrong and Small (2010) investigated rural women's perspectives on postnatal depression screening, highlighting the paradox of screening, as published in BMC Public Health. 11. Buist et al. (2006) assessed the acceptability of routine screening for perinatal depression in their study published in the Journal of Affective Disorders. 12. Waqas et al. critically reviewed and conducted a meta-analysis on the prevention of common mental disorders among perinatal women, with findings in press in Global Mental Health. 13. Dukhovny et al. (2013) evaluated the economic impact of a peer support intervention aimed at preventing postpartum depression in high-risk women in Ontario, Canada, as published in the American Journal of Perinatology. 14. Ride et al. (2016) analyzed the cost-effectiveness of a psychoeducational intervention to prevent postnatal maternal mental health problems, published in BMJ Open. 15. Delaney, George Dalmida, and Gaydos (2015) explored the mental health needs of mothers beyond postpartum depression in their publication in Issues in Mental Health Nursing. 16. Raymond et al. (2014) conducted a focus group study addressing perinatal depression among underserved urban women, published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth. 17. Thurtle (2003) examined first-time mothers' perceptions of motherhood and postnatal depression in Community Practitioner. 18. The WHO (2016) provided guidelines on iron supplementation for postpartum women. 19. The WHO (2016) also issued recommendations for daily iron supplementation in adult women and adolescent girls. 20. The WHO (2011) published guidelines on intermittent iron and folic acid supplementation for menstruating women. 21. The WHO (2011) outlined hemoglobin concentration thresholds for diagnosing anemia and assessing its severity. 22. The International Nutritional Anemia Consultative Group, WHO, and UNICEF (1998) provided guidelines for using iron supplements to prevent and treat iron deficiency anemia. 23. The WHO (2001) published a booklet for mothers on healthy eating during pregnancy and breastfeeding. 24. The WHO (2011) issued recommendations on vitamin A supplementation for postpartum women. 25. The WHO (2020) released guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior. 26. The WHO (2014) provided guidance on ensuring human rights in the provision of contraceptive information and services. 27. The WHO (2015) outlined medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use. 28. The WHO (2019) addressed contraceptive eligibility for women at high risk of HIV. 29. The WHO (2019) consolidated guidelines on self-care interventions for sexual and reproductive health and rights. 30. Rahi and Gilbert (2017) discussed the global impact of visual impairment in children in the sixth edition of Taylor and Hoyt’s Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus. 31. 32. Malik et al. reviewed international guidelines on universal newborn eye screening in a systematic review. 33. Lieu et al. (2020) reviewed the epidemiology and impact of hearing loss in children, published in JAMA. 34. Butcher et al. (2019) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence of permanent childhood hearing loss detected through universal newborn hearing screening, published in PLoS One. 35. The WHO (2021) released the World Report on Hearing. 36. Bhutani et al. (2013) estimated the global incidence and impact of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and Rhesus disease of the newborn, published in Pediatric Research. 37. Olusanya, Kaplan, and Hansen (2018) provided a global perspective on neonatal hyperbilirubinemia in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health. 38. Sun et al. evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of the red reflex test in newborn eye screening, published in the Journal of Pediatrics. 39. Haargaard et al. (2015) analyzed the age of detection for congenital cataracts in the Pediatric Cataract Register (PECaR), published in Acta Ophthalmologica. 40. Magnusson and Persson (2005) conducted a cost-consequence analysis of congenital cataract screening at maternity wards versus well-baby clinics, published in Acta Paediatrica. 41. The American Academy of Pediatrics (2008) provided guidelines on red reflex examination in neonates, infants, and children. 42. UNICEF's supply catalog provides resources for maternal and child health, accessed in January 2022. 43. Lowe et al. (2015) evaluated the Arclight ophthalmoscope as a low-cost alternative to standard direct ophthalmoscopes, published in the Journal of Ophthalmology. 44. Kong et al. (2012) reviewed progress and changes in the epidemiology of childhood blindness worldwide, published in the Journal of AAPOS. 45. Gilbert and Lepvrier-Chomette (2016) reviewed gender inequalities in bilateral cataract surgery among children in low-income countries, published in Ophthalmology. 46. The Global Retinoblastoma Study Group (2020) analyzed retinoblastoma presentation by national income level, published in JAMA Oncology. 47. Malik et al. (2020) studied the integration of eye health training into primary child healthcare programs in Tanzania, published in BMJ Paediatrics Open. 48. Mndeme et al. (2021) evaluated the feasibility and diagnostic accuracy of red reflex examination for early detection of pediatric cataracts in Tanzania, published in Eye. 49. The Universal Newborn Hearing Screening (UNHS) review group is preparing a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effectiveness of UNHS. 50. Nelson et al. (2008) updated the 2001 US Preventive Services Task Force recommendations on universal newborn hearing screening, published in Pediatrics. 51. Patel et al. (2011) discussed universal newborn hearing screening in Paediatrics & Child Health. 52. Sharma et al. (2019) conducted a systematic review and critique of economic evaluations of childhood hearing loss screening programs, published in Applied Health Economics. 53. Olusanya et al. (2009) analyzed the costs and performance of early hearing detection programs in Lagos, Nigeria, published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 54. Heidari et al. (2017) conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of automated auditory brainstem response and otoacoustic emission in universal neonatal hearing screening, published in the Iranian Journal of Pediatrics. 55. Gupta et al. (2015) highlighted challenges in implementing universal newborn hearing screening at a tertiary care center in India, published in the Indian Journal of Pediatrics. 56. Verkleij et al. (2021) used micro-simulation modeling to analyze the cost-effectiveness of neonatal hearing screening programs, published in Ear and Hearing. 57. Coates and Gifkins (2003) discussed newborn hearing screening in the Australian Prescriber. 58. Olusanya and Newton (2007) reviewed the global burden of childhood hearing impairment and disease control priorities for developing countries, published in The Lancet. 59. Van Kerschaver et al. (2012) studied socio-demographic determinants of hearing impairment in term babies, published in the European Journal of Public Health. 60. Lantos et al. (2018) examined geographic and racial disparities in infant hearing loss, published in Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery. 61. Frary et al. (2020) identified risk factors for non-participation in the Danish universal newborn hearing screening program, published in the International Journal of Pediatric Otorhinolaryngology. 62. Young and Tattersall (2005) evaluated parents' experiences with universal newborn hearing screening, published in the Journal of Deaf Studies and Deaf Education. 63. Young and Tattersall (2007) explored parents' responses to early identification of deafness and their expectations for child communication development, published in the Journal of Deaf Studies and Deaf Education. 64. Bass et al. (2006) provided stakeholder recommendations for parent-centered communication in infant hearing screening, published in Pediatrics. 65. Jatto et al. (2018) examined mothers' perspectives on newborn hearing screening programs, published in the Ghana Medical Journal. 66. The WHO (2017) issued recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience.
